notes.title: Dev Diary #6: Game Update
notes.content:
So it's been a while since the last Dev Diary and I thought it'd be a great time to update everyone about what's been going on and share some screenshots.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/7648e81f1bd05a75d15602613c01cd6ce928959b.png

The game is progressing fine and I've mostly been tweaking and optimizing. One big feature that was completed recently is the Battle Simulator.
The simulator spawns random battles with random heroes against random enemies and will be covered in more detail in a later Dev Diary. 
If you're just want to have some fun in a quick skirmish, the Battle Simulator is where to click. 

As mentioned in the trailers, I've always wanted a HUGE fantasy world to explore and travel. After playing around with different sizes, I settled on a 2500 (50 x 50) hexagonal grid.
This gives me enough room to play with and doesn't bunch everything up. It also makes the game world feel bigger and more epic.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/6e936056c52eaabb6775343c3517a2ce16a4247b.png

But the problem with having a world that large is performance. The more you put on the screen, the worse performance will be. 
Many games solve this problem by limiting what's visible or being rendered at any one time. The content is restricted to one level, one town, one can only zoom so far, etc.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/0b6b0c9925cf620d64a5bb6ae6056a196e338805.png

These optimizations I also implemented but wasn't too happy with them. I wanted the player to be able to zoom out and see the entire game world in all its glory.
I wanted to be able to put as many details on the screen without compromising on performance.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/25121adad74ade164cf7edcb202de240a391aac5.png

Previously this was not possible and the more that was rendered, the more the frame rate dropped. So with a lot of optimization, tweaking and caching, I set about improving performance.
That was the goal of the last few weeks and I think I may have achieved it. I've included some screenshots of the current look and feel of the game world. 
Don't worry, no spoilers here. This is just a draft and does not represent the final map at all. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/70dfd588e9275b0f33b87eb0ad97d1eadcf94e87.png

But I thought it important enough to share and I hope it will give potential players a better overview of what this game is about. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/a680dfa55b6f538207b6ea42b1c2cf946dcb13b7.png

I also spent some time improving the game world look. Adding things like rivers, bridges and creating a more natural looking landscape. 
Before the grid tiles looked too circular and artificial. With a little bit of adjustment, they now appear more real and natural.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/983903ac53306489ccd50ad6fd52c4cb2700e0c8.png

All that being said, the entire game world can now be rendered and I consistently reach a FPS of 110 - 120 on normal graphic settings. 
True, I am running this on a NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 but I'm hoping even older cards will be able to achieve at least 60 FPS.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/4e27f1992edb7ea61d41b096daaf08ab0988da7a.png

On a different note, I've also decided to rearrange the Chapters a bit and include three Chapters in the Early Access Game instead of two. This will expand the game play by about 10 - 20 hours.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/7deaefea66bd89ca6911d41291f87b019f8799be.png

As always, thanks for reading this far and more Dev Diaries will be coming shortly.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/0aac04a6424bb91c3fbbe3568c13e8c34f916c67.png

notes.title: Dev Diary #5 - The Hero Party
notes.content:
So how do your Heroes get around the game world?

Well, there are actually 2 ways, they can walk or they can travel in style as part of a Hero Party.

Walking is an old fashioned mode of transportation. It takes longer, is more tiring and your Hero is more prone to attack.
A walking Hero can only cover 1 map grid per turn. The physical strain keeps his health from recovering and saps his morale.
And if by chance he is attacked by wandering Goblins or other nasties, only other Heroes in the same map grid can help.

The preferred mode of transport for your Heroes is the Hero Party. Your Heroes travel the land in style in their Hero Party Wagon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/721e0bd3a26c2e2b1940e08a1686c442d5a32844.png

Not only is it faster and can travel 3 map grids per turn but it can also carry up to 6 Heroes.

Heroes in a party can rest and recover health. Morale also will not suffer. In case it's attacked, all Heroes in the party take part in the battle. Furthermore a Hero Party can carry Cargo such as Potions or other goods.  

Creating a Hero Party

Hero Parties can be created from any town or castle. Since a Wagon is required, only these locations can create them. 

Once a Hero Party is created though, the Wagon belongs to it and can be reused. If your Hero Party travels to a location the Wagon stays there while your party camps in the area.

The party can continue its travels once they are ready again. Only dissolving a Hero Party will destroy the Wagon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/3aa11fa3407a7010f38894f7ac0d30ef158ae61b.png

You can think of the Hero Party as individual transport units. Once created, use them to transport your Heroes from location to location.

A quest needs to be completed, send a Hero Party. Famine in town, send a Hero Party. Goblin Raiders or a Golem need to be intercepted, Hero Party! And so on.

Hero Parties appear on the left side of the screen with the Avatar of the first Hero in that party. Hovering over it will reveal all the Heroes in that party.

Clicking on any of the Avatars will center the screen on the party. 
And clicking on the parchment icon to the right of the avatars will open the Hero Party Settings.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/9077c5ca81ea3a80e195b5efed56c336aff58599.png

Hero Party Settings

The settings gives you a detail view of the party and allow you to manage it. 

Here you can: 


 Take a look at its Heroes and their Stats / Skills
 Transfer Cargo between the party, its current location and your Warehouse
 Transfer Heroes between the party and its current location
 Split the party up into a new one
 Merge it with other Hero Parties at that location
 Dissolve the party and return its Cargo and Heroes to the current location


In this screen you can take a look at all the Heroes in the party, their Stats and Skills

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/97835ae728f99da83cec92b413eae21545cdfd02.png

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In this screen you can transfer cargo between the Hero Party, the Market and your Warehouse at that location

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/e6e758f240d520dd6bff0b873475befeae7e1624.png

If the location is a POI (Point of Interest) like a town or castle, Cargo can be bought or sold at the market.

You can also transfer Cargo to your Warehouse. You have a Warehouse at each POI in the game world which has unlimited capacity but the more you store, the more it costs per turn.

Unfriendly locations such as caves, tombs, dungeons etc. do not have Markets or a Warehouse.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In this screen you can transfer Heroes between the party and its current location

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/4670acca48084b1a898940b779db4ba48cedf901.png

Heroes can be transferred from the party to the location and as long as it has capacity, back to the Hero Party.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Splitting and Merging a Hero Party are still being developed and might even be eventually removed (we'll see)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

And last, in this screen you can dissolve the Hero Party. Dissolving means all Heroes and Cargo will be transferred to the current location.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/8a242b1dedc759382c02dfc4a5efc356d02b334c.png

The Hero Party loses its Wagon and can no longer travel around the game world. 

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In conclusion, thanks for reading this Dev Diary to the end. I hope it has given you a better understanding of the game mechanics. 

My hope with this mechanic was to create a sense of adventure. You get a quest, pack your Heroes into their wagon and off they go!

notes.title: State of the Game
notes.content:
State of the Game

Just wanted to post an update about the current state of the game and when Early Access will be available.

The last few weeks and months I have been play testing and polishing the game. 

Somethings I am happy with, others not so much. My goal the entire time has been to create a fun game the player can escape a few hours with.

In that regard, the game is mostly successful. You begin the game with a few quests, recruit your heroes, send them out to explore, fight battles and complete quests.

For successful quests, you get rewarded and can expand. 

If you're unable to complete quests then you won't get rewarded and eventually run out of gold to recruit new heroes.

This does not necessarily mean you lose. Your heroes will slowly regain health and can still be sent on quests. You can also trade to boost your income. But there is a chance that you run out of heroes / gold and have to face the music.

So there is a bit of risk in the game and you do have to think about which quests to accept / complete and who to send on them.

So far, so good. 

But as with most games, this becomes repetitive and a bit tedious. There will be different chapters to complete which introduce new content but I'm trying to think of something bigger.

You have your private army of heroes and what else can you do with them?

I'm thinking that eventually you will have to side with one of the Factions (Human, Elven, Goblin or Undead) and wage war against the others for control of the world but this still needs to be fleshed out.

So I'm trying to keep the game engaging even in the later stages.

What's currently being worked on

- Parts of the UI seem a little dated and I want to improve / upgrade those
- Adding more Character Skills and Spells (especially for Archer / Mage / Cleric)
- Adding more Accessories to make character customization even more unique
- Bug fixing 

Introducing deeper battles

As you've perhaps seen from the trailers and screenshots, the battles are fought on a square-like battle board. 

This allows for some strategic variations such as structures, barriers, wave battles, etc. But it's also limited and the battles eventually become repetitive.

With this in mind, I want to expand the battles for certain locations. For example, if there is a unique location like a dungeon or tomb, this should be something bigger. There should be multiple rooms / areas that have to be explored with multiple enemies to be slayed along with an end boss.

So this is being currently worked on and will be introduced as soon as possible.


When will Early Access be available?

This is a little difficult to say at the moment. I don't want to commit myself to a date and then not be able to deliver or deliver a shoddy product. Anyone remember Sword of the Stars II?

I want to release a polished game with enough content. Let's say a rough estimate will be the next 6 - 12 months. In the meantime, I will keep posting updates and dev diaries about new features and content.

I'm currently not active on Discord and maybe I should be. But from what I've heard, Discord is a real time-sink and at the moment I'm not able to spend that much time on it.

As always, I'll keep posting new announcements on Steam and if you have questions or comments that's where I'm the most active.

And thanks for reading to the end ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Dev Diary #4 - Hero Recruitment, Part 1
notes.content:
Overview

Recruiting Heroes is one of the primary functions in F-Team. Heroes are the bread and butter of your business and necessary to 


 fight battles
 fulfill quests
 garrison locations
 buy, sell and transport goods

It is up to you to make your Heroes as individual and unique as possible. The point here is not to  generate cookie-cutter type Heroes which are fed into the meat grinder of battle.

Give them unique names, avatars, colors and accessories. Your Heroes are your creation and should be treated as valuable assets vital to your success.

Or not. Perhaps you prefer to spam Heroes and only the ones which survive the test of battle are truly worthy to stand in your team.

The choice is yours.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/6c97a3897b448d90a37dc736fc22dd45d4629d93.png

Hero Recruitment

Heroes can be recruited in two different ways. The first and simpler way is directly hiring a Hero from the tavern. Each castle, town and stronghold has a tavern and occasionally Heroes for hire will appear and offer their services for a price. If you have a spy in that location, you will automatically be notified of this. 

Heroes for hire are experienced warriors with numerous learned Skills. They are usually worth their price, if you can afford them.

The other and more common way is to recruit Heroes yourself.  Each location ( castle, town, stronghold ) will have a number of recruits willing to become Heroes. Castles have more recruits than Strongholds which have more recruits than towns. 

You can recruit Heroes from the main menu or from the location menu. 

Recruitment Screen

The Recruitment Screen is where you recruit and customize your Heroes. The left side of the screen contains class, avatar, name, stats and costs. 

The right side of the screen contains various customization categories, such as armor, weapon, shield, armor / hair / skin color, accessories and so on.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/484633075e30fad7eebc8c4218d3ce694a79030e.png

Hero Classes

There are currently 6 classes of Heroes to choose from:


 Fighter
 Archer
 Mage
 Ranger
 Knight
 Cleric


The fighter is a tried and true Hero. Good overall stats with the ability to yield most weapons and shields. Unable to cast magic or perform ranged attack, he can however master various melee fighting skills.

The archer prefers his more civilized methods of pacification. Weaker than the fighter but skilled in the art of ranged combat, he can render devastating damage from a distance, without ever dirtying his own hands.

The mage is a master of the arcane arts. Unlike his more physical colleagues, the mage prefers skill and intelligence to rule the battlefield. The mage makes up his weakness in melee attack through his command of offensive magic.

The ranger offers a mix of classes. Not as strong as a fighter but more agile, the ranger possesses skills in melee combat and the arcane arts. Able to move farther and poison opponents the ranger can also call upon the forces of nature to do his bidding.

The knight is an upgrade to the fighter. Stronger than his fighter cousin the knight can wear heavier armor and yield weapons such as great swords, great axes and great hammers. Unable to command magic, this tank can however take and deal the damage.

The cleric is the weakest of the classes. Not possessing many offensive abilities the cleric's main task is supportive. His is the only class capable of learning buff and mass buff spells to help his colleagues in combat.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/86c9d3e0b80c4310428b530ffdfd641786d33736.png

Hero Stats

Your Hero consists of 9 Stats:


 Hit Points
 Attack
 Defense
 Strength
 Agility
 Intelligence
 Luck
 Morale
 Stamina

The stats vary between classes with certain ones such as fighter and knight having higher attack, defense and strength stats and others such as mage, archer, ranger and cleric having higher agility, luck and intelligence.

As your Hero gains in experience and reaches new levels, each Stat can be increased by learning a new Stat Skill.

Hit Points determine how long your Hero lasts in battle. As your Hero takes damage his Hit Points will decrease. Once they reach 0, your Hero is defeated and deceased. Death is permanent and your Hero will no longer be available.

Hit Points can be raised by taking health potions or through Heal and Mass Heal spells provided by a cleric. Hit Points will also gradually recover turn-by-turn after a battle.


 Attack determines how much damage your Hero deals in battle. The higher the Attack, the more the damage.
 Defense determines how much damage your Hero absorbs in battle. The higher the Defense, the less the damage.
 Strength is a very important Stat. It not only determines how much damage your Hero does but also how much armor and which weapons your Hero can yield.
 Agility determines how far your Hero moves in battle and the chance for misses. The higher the Agility, the greater the chance your Hero will evade damage.
 Intelligence is very important in learning new Skills. The higher the Intelligence, the less time it will take to learn new Skills.
 Luck determines the chances for misses in battle. Combined with Agility, the higher the Luck, the greater the chance your Hero will evade damage.
 Morale determines the courage of your Hero in battle. A high morale will keep them in the fight. But the more damage your Hero takes, the lower their morale will fall. A Hero with low morale is more likely to panic.

And lastly, Stamina. Stamina determines how much fight your Hero has in battle. Each attack and Skill requires a certain amount of Stamina to perform.

Based on their Stamina, your Hero can perform multiple actions per turn. This allows for interesting combinations and requires you to coordinate attacks.

Stamina is recovered each turn in battle and can be increased by taking stamina potions, through Skill training or buff spells.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/66724cb6b1a8118e2b1c9cabd7e6892a7c751647.png

notes.title: Dev Diary #3 - The Tavern
notes.content:
The Tavern

In each castle, town and stronghold throughout the land, the player will find a tavern filled with interesting patrons. As you travel the land and discover these locations, you'll be able to visit their taverns and interact with their guests.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/4de6c61bae69a9c0a365350df93b634b4c0e3867.png

Currently there are 5 types of patrons to find at the tavern:

Quest Giver
Hero for Hire
Location Giver
Spy
Treasure Hunter


Quest Giver

As the name suggests, the Quest Giver will offer you quests to fulfill. These will be your primary source of income and allow you to recruit new heroes, train them, trade at the market and so on. The Quest Giver will remain at the tavern for a certain period of time and then disappear. Some quest givers will only appear at certain locations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/376125e7b602e37021f8f67cddc46d5f99008c43.png

Hero for Hire

These heroes can be hired instead of recruited. They are experienced warriors looking for a new liege. Since they already come with skills and a certain level, the hiring cost is usually steep. After hiring, the hero can be further customized and naturally they will continue to gain in experience and level.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/0b39928a230f8d75fb78e1c1ed9cc199769daba2.png

Location Giver

These patrons will offer you the location of a Point of Interest, naturally for a price. Some locations will only be discoverable through a Location Giver. Or perhaps you are simply interested in knowing where a certain location is. Furthermore, uncovering these places will trigger new quests.

Spy

Spies are an important function of the game and the only way to gain information about what's going on in the world. For example, if Goblin Raiders or Ice Beasts have appeared and are on a rampage. Or if a location is about to attacked. It's important to have spies telling you these things.

Treasure Hunter

There are those in this world who seek treasure but are too afraid to get it themselves. They will offer a part of it, if you find it for them. For a price, the treasure hunter will offer you a map. You will have to send a Hero Party there and deal with any opposition. If successful, you will discover the treasure and receive part of it.

notes.title: Dev Diary # 2 - Points of Interest
notes.content:
Points of Interest

The game world is designed to resemble a tabletop board game. Scattered around the world are various Points of Interest (POIs) which the player can interact with. They are divided into three categories, friendly, unfriendly and production.

Friendly POIs

These include locations such as castles, strongholds and towns. Here the player can rest his heroes, recruit new ones, visit the tavern or market, train his heroes and so on. These are the only locations where new heroes can be recruited. 

At the tavern the player will find new quests, can hire already experienced heroes, buy information or hire spies / informants. The Market was already covered in Dev Diary # 1 and Hero Training and Spies / Informants will be covered in the future.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/e0c7b9f5ea4d997ab3b975b4c0e978c57d9d5cf5.png

Unfriendly POIs

Naturally the world is not without danger and risk. These POIs should be approached with extreme caution; if a Hero Party should venture too closely they may be attacked the following turn. And many quests will arise from these locations as the player is tasked with defeating the enemies within.

Furthermore, the locations present the opportunity for looting. Some high-value items such as spider fangs or mushrooms can only be gained from looting POIs such as spider caves or the dead forest of an evil witch.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/7bf2bb1fef41649da83e281bbe3ba9efdbcc7d3d.png

Production POIs

As the name suggests, these are neutral locations and exist solely to produce resources. These resources are needed for quests or can be traded. Some quests will require the player to garrison heroes here to protect them from future attacks. Heroes quartering at these locations will also be able to rest, recovering both hit points and morale.

These POIs are also based on race. Each race will have unique POIs located only within their lands. Humans will have ones such as gold and iron mines, Goblins will have gem mines and bone yards, and so on. Same for the the Elves and the Undead.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/c895a5d8f90c3bad7a43e0cb543fb375a2deb454.png

List of current Points of Interest

 Gem, gold and iron mines

notes.title: Dev Diary # 1 - The Market
notes.content:
Market Items

The market is based on simple economics, buying and selling. High-value items such as gold or gems will have a higher price than more common items like bread or cheese. And items in Capitals will fetch a higher price than in towns. Also, as the quantity of a item decreases, its price will increase and vice-versa. 

In the game there are 4 races (Human, Elves, Goblins and the Undead) controlling the world. Each race offers unique items to buy, loot and trade. Some items will be shared between the races but most will be unique to that race. This opens up the possibility of trade between races where sought-after items from one race can be sold for high profit elsewhere.

Of course, shipments of expensive cargo will always be ripe for attack from goblin raiders, brigands and others, so make sure they have adequate protection.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/5f7aa38395932c5458abb93376259b585f9c31de.png

Points of Interest

Scattered throughout the game world are various Points of Interests (POIs). These include not only capitals and towns but also mines, caves, tombs, productions facilities and so on. Some POIs will produce items at low cost which can then be sold at other locations for a large profit. These locations will initially be hidden and can be discovered by exploring or by buying information at taverns. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/391d234a4e9e41cebffe26046be80fa1b1305f06.png

Some items will only be obtainable from certain POIs. For example, iron and gold are only available at iron and gold mines. Spider fangs can only be looted from spider caves and ice cubes can only be found amongst the remains of Ice Beasts. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/2dafed662a0346a4e07cc39417dbd0de7274bc2d.png

Item Quests

This also opens up the possibility of various quests such as transport, fetch, gather and loot quests. 
Transport quests will require the player to transport goods from one location to another
Fetch quests will require the player to fetch an certain item of importance such as a weapon, jewel, relic, etc.Gather quests will require the player to gather a certain amount of items and transport them within a limited amount of turnsLoot quests will require the player to travel to a location and do battle. The player can then return the loot for a reward or keep it for themselves.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/141e66b3ee68e2436f7287259a6769be4be48e77.png
